title: Tell the on-call engineer which thread everyone waits for

blocks.text: The payments service hangs a few times a month, and each time the on-call engineer scrolls through a `jcmd <pid> Thread.print` of four hundred threads, looking for the one that everybody else is waiting for. The dump has no deadlock section, because there is no cycle. We want a tool that reads the dump and answers that question directly.
`DumpReader` already splits a dump into threads and joins the answers into a report. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/DumpReader.java`:

items: `waitingFor(thread)`: the monitor the thread is blocked trying to enter, or `null`;
`held(thread)`: the monitors the thread holds while the dump is taken.

blocks.text: When you're done, `whoBlocksWhom(dump)` maps each thread that is blocked on a `synchronized` lock to the threads that really hold that lock, and to no one else. Threads that sleep, park or wait for a notify are not blocked by anybody. About fifteen lines in total, including any helper you add to read a lock line.
The tests feed it thread blocks cut from a real Java 21 dump of a payments program, so print one with `jcmd` from a small program of your own if you want to see every kind of line first.

cases.says: a thread blocked at a synchronized block is reported with the thread that holds that lock
a dump whose threads only park on a latch reports no one as blocked
a thread inside wait() is not reported as holding the monitor it waits on, though its stack lists it as locked
a thread inside wait() is not reported as blocked by whoever holds that monitor
a thread waiting for one object is charged to that object's holder, not to a thread holding another object of the same class
a thread holding nested locks is reported for every one of them

origin.section: A Thread Dump Names a Deadlock Cycle, Not a Thread Stuck Behind a Holder That Waits

concepts: A thread BLOCKED on a monitor names the object's address; the thread whose stack lists that address as locked is the one it waits for, and two objects of one class are two locks.
A thread keeps its monitors while it parks, sleeps or reads; only Object.wait() gives up the one it waits on, though the dump still lists it as locked below a waiting-on line.
